dist/research/index.html.beforeMain:
01 / Research

Authorization as a research question.

From deterministic access rules to explainable, policy-bounded adaptation. A research program grounded in comparison, transparency and reproducibility.

The problem

Decisions in changing systems.

Research Problem

Cloud-native distributed systems make access decisions while identities, request context and operational conditions change. Roles and attributes provide explicit policy boundaries, but understanding how authorization should respond to abnormal behavior remains a research challenge.

AeglysAI investigates whether behavioral evidence and operational system state can inform useful adaptations while preserving deterministic constraints and understandable decisions. The benefits and tradeoffs remain to be tested.

Research Question

How does explainable, policy-bounded, closed-loop adaptive authorization perform relative to RBAC, ABAC and deterministic risk-aware authorization under behavioral and operational anomalies in cloud-native distributed systems?

Comparative foundation

Baselines

Implementation status refers to the separate AeglysAI research/application repository. This portal presents the research program.

Model AA

RBAC

Role-based access control establishes the deterministic authorization baseline.

Implemented
Model BB

RBAC + ABAC

Attribute-based conditions extend role-based authorization with request context.

Implemented
Model CC

Contextual Risk

Deterministic contextual risk adds explicit risk rules to role-based authorization.

Implemented
Bounded offline research

Model D — Research Implementation Complete

Research Implementation Complete

The bounded offline research implementation is complete; internal synthetic validation has been performed. Model D remains experimental and non-enforcing.

Completed work includes offline behavioral inference, eligibility and drift diagnostics, experimental integration, mock-feedback simulation and internal reproducibility checks. These research capabilities do not grant or deny access.

enforcement_authority=NONE. Internal synthetic validation does not establish external field effectiveness, production authorization capability or commercial readiness. Drift coverage and mock-feedback effectiveness limitations remain unresolved.

Local engineering acceptance is not independent field validation, security/distribution clearance or a commercial product release. No model artifacts, datasets or internal evaluation results are published here.

How we investigate

Research Principles

01

Policy remains explicit

Investigate adaptation constrained by deterministic rules and reviewable decision boundaries.

02

Evidence before claims

Separate implemented capabilities, planned designs and experimentally supported findings.

03

Explain the decision

Make the contributing policy, context and proposed risk evidence understandable to reviewers.

Open methodology

Reproducibility

The intended experimental program compares models under documented scenarios and controlled conditions. Methods, configurations and limitations should accompany results so others can assess and reproduce the work.

(() => {
  const key = 'aeglysai-theme';
  const root = document.documentElement;
  const system = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');
  let preference = null;
  try {
    const stored = localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (stored === 'light' || stored === 'dark') preference = stored;
  } catch { /* Theme still works when storage is unavailable. */ }
  const apply = () => {
    const theme = preference || (system.matches ? 'dark' : 'light');
    root.dataset.theme = theme;
    root.dataset.themePreference = preference || 'system';
    const meta = document.querySelector('meta[name="theme-color"]');
    if (meta) meta.setAttribute('content', theme === 'dark' ? '#080f1c' : '#f6f7f9');
    const toggle = document.querySelector('[data-theme-toggle]');
    const reset = document.querySelector('[data-theme-system]');
    if (toggle) {
      const label = `Switch to ${theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'} theme`;
      toggle.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
      toggle.setAttribute('title', label);
      toggle.hidden = false;
    }
    if (reset) {
      reset.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(preference === null));
      reset.setAttribute('title', preference === null ? 'System theme active' : 'Use system theme');
      reset.hidden = false;
    }
  };
  apply();
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
    apply();
    const choose = (value) => {
      preference = value;
      try { value ? localStorage.setItem(key, value) : localStorage.removeItem(key); } catch {}
      apply();
      const status = document.querySelector('[data-theme-status]');
      if (status) status.textContent = `${root.dataset.theme} theme${value ? '' : ' (system default)'}`;
    };
    document.querySelector('[data-theme-toggle]')?.addEventListener('click', () => choose(root.dataset.theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'));
    document.querySelector('[data-theme-system]')?.addEventListener('click', () => choose(null));
  }, { once: true });
  system.addEventListener('change', () => { if (preference === null) apply(); });
  window.addEventListener('storage', (event) => {
    if (event.key === key || event.key === null) {
      preference = event.newValue === 'light' || event.newValue === 'dark' ? event.newValue : null;
      apply();
    }
  });
})();

02 / Architecture

Explicit policy. Informed decisions.

A conceptual view of the authorization path and the research extensions that could connect evidence, bounded decisions and continuous feedback.

Research completion does not grant enforcement

Model D research implementation is complete for its bounded offline experimental scope. The diagram separates the implemented baseline path, completed offline research and planned operational extensions. It is not an implemented adaptive enforcement path. enforcement_authority=NONE; external validation, drift and mock-feedback limitations remain.

01

Deterministic Policy

Role-based authorization and attribute conditions provide explicit rules in the implemented baselines. They form the foundation for investigating policy-bounded adaptation.

Implemented
02

Contextual Risk

Model C uses deterministic contextual risk. This rule-based capability is distinct from learned behavioral anomaly detection.

Implemented
03

Behavioral Intelligence

Completed offline experimental behavioral inference and bounded eligibility/drift diagnostics produce evidence, not access decisions. Internal synthetic checks do not establish external effectiveness or mature drift monitoring.

Research Implementation Complete
04

Experimental Recommendation Integration

Completed offline research integration produces non-enforcing recommendations. Model D has enforcement_authority=NONE; production adaptive decisions remain a planned extension.

Research Implementation Complete
05

Mock Feedback and Future Live Feedback

In-memory mock-feedback simulation is implemented for offline research; response effectiveness remains unestablished. Live telemetry and continuous production feedback are planned extensions, with stability and operational costs unresolved.

Planned Research

A map of the investigation

The diagram distinguishes existing baseline capabilities, completed offline experimental research and proposed operational extensions. It does not specify deployed services, live telemetry coverage or an implemented production adaptive decision engine.

An engineering origin. A research direction.

AeglysAI grows from a microservices security project into a research program exploring adaptive intelligence for secure distributed systems.

AeglysAI is the evolution of the research initiative previously known as AegisAI.

The person behind the project

Creator & Maintainer

Shubh Prabhat

Solution Architect

Creator & Maintainer, AeglysAI

AI-Driven Automation for Resilient and Secure Cloud & Distributed Systems

Shubh Prabhat is a solution architect whose technical interests span cloud-native architecture, microservices, identity and authorization, network automation, resilient systems, and AI-driven automation.

He created the initiative previously known as AegisAI and maintains it as AeglysAI, an open-source research initiative for investigating explainable, risk-aware and adaptive authorization in cloud-native distributed systems.
